drivingQuestion: Is the mishna's ruling that one letter invalidates the mezuza not obvious?
outcomeNote: The redundancy objection is answered in the next unit (menachot.sugya088).

segments.he: שְׁתֵּי פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת שֶׁבַּמְּזוּזָה מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ, וַאֲפִילּוּ כְּתָב אֶחָד מְעַכְּבָן. פְּשִׁיטָא!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: With regard to the «two passages that are in the mezuza,» the absence of «each prevents fulfillment of the mitzva with the others. And» furthermore, the absence of «even one letter prevents fulfillment of the mitzva with» the rest of «them.» The Gemara asks: Isn’t it «obvious» that the absence of even one letter prevents fulfillment of the mitzva, since it is written: “And you shall write them [ukhtavtam]” (Deuteronomy 6:9), which teaches that the writing [ketav] must be complete [tam]?
